title: Through my fault
hookLine: the whole church admits it has sinned and asks each other for prayer

lines: A MEETING THAT STARTS WITH SORRY.
cards: A staff meeting begins. Everyone stands up, the boss included, and says out loud, together: I've messed up. In what I thought, what I said, what I did, and what I didn't do.
It's my fault. Then everyone turns to the people around them and says: please pray for me. It would be the strangest meeting of the year.
And it's roughly what can happen in the first minutes of a Catholic Mass. Right after the greeting, before a single reading, the whole church owns up.

teach.b: It's called the Confiteor, from its first word in Latin: I confess. The priest invites everyone to call their sins to mind, and there's a short silence.

Then priest and people together say they confess to almighty God, and to each other, that they have greatly sinned, in their thoughts and in their words, in what they have done and in what they have failed to do.
That last part is sharp: not just the wrong things, but the good things left undone.

teach.h: MEA CULPA, AND A FIST ON THE CHEST.
teach.b: Then comes the line, in the old Latin: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa. Through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. As they say it, people strike their chest with a closed hand.

That gesture echoes a story Jesus told. A tax collector stands at the back of the Temple, won't even lift his eyes, beats his breast and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner."
Jesus says that man went home right with God. Then the Confiteor turns outward.

teach.h: PRAY FOR ME, BROTHERS AND SISTERS.
teach.b: Everyone asks Mary, the angels and the saints, and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me. You confess to the people beside you, and then you ask them for help. Nobody stands above anybody; the priest says it too.

teach.h: O GOD, BE MERCIFUL TO ME A SINNER.
teach.b: The Church is clear that this isn't the sacrament of confession, and doesn't replace it. It's a way of starting honestly.
Looking back over this week, from bending the knee to the Angelus to the entrance, the body keeps saying things before words do. Here, it's a fist on the chest.

how: At the start of most Masses, after a brief silence, priest and people pray the Confiteor together, many striking their breast at 'through my fault'; it is one of several forms of the penitential act and does not replace the sacrament of confession.

games.q: what's inside the prayer — tap the pairs.

s: the Confiteor replaces going to confession
the Church is clear it's not the sacrament of confession. it's a way of starting Mass honestly.

games.q: you're the tax collector at the back of the Temple. you can't even lift your eyes. what do you do?
o: list your good deeds to balance things out.
beat your breast and ask God for mercy.
games.why: he beat his breast and said: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner." Jesus says he went home right with God. the fist on the chest at Mass echoes him.

practice: Look back over the last day or two, not to punish yourself, just to see clearly: one thing you did that you wish you hadn't, one thing you left undone.
If you're Catholic, or you'd like to, you can strike your chest gently, once, the way the tax collector did, and if you pray, you can use his words. If not, just name it, and set it down.
